events.extended_summary: The Trump administration announced new tariffs under Section 338 of the 1930s Smoot-Hawley Act, replacing previous findings on forced labour provisions. The rates take effect in January or February after consultation, lacking the fanfare of April 2025's "Liberation Day" tariffs. The move shores up the domestic legal basis after the Supreme Court struck down the original emergency basis earlier this year, creating two legal bases for many countries. The UK remains unaffected but stays subject to forced labour provisions at a 10% rate on global tariffs, with no move against its digital services tax. Twenty-five states have sued to strike down the forced labour tariffs. Half of Canada's tariffs are authorized under Section 338. The tariffs must be finalized under a Democrat Congress, where a Senate bill exists and rebel Republicans could potentially override a presidential veto.
events.micro_summary: Trump announces new tariffs under Section 338 replacing forced labour provisions, effective January or February after consultation.
events.summary: The Trump administration announced new tariffs under Section 338 of the 1930s Smoot-Hawley Act to replace forced labour provisions, with rates effective January or February after consultation, following the Supreme Court striking down the original emergency basis earlier this year.

events.extended_summary: The European Union is engaged in contentious budget negotiations, with leaders meeting November 26-27 to decide on a €45 billion ($49 billion) loan to Ukraine and the 2028-2034 budget. The talks pit net contributors like Germany against recipients such as Poland and Hungary, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to veto the EU budget unless all members back the Ukraine loan, which requires unanimous approval. The IMF estimates Ukraine's funding gap at €70 billion ($76 billion) for the coming year. The draft budget earmarks €100 billion for Ukraine, but disputes persist over whether €55.4 billion in interest payments on existing loans are included or paid separately, with Italy and Bulgaria questioning the arrangement.
events.micro_summary: EU leaders meet November 26-27 to decide on €45 billion Ukraine loan and 2028-2034 budget.
events.summary: EU leaders meet November 26-27 to decide on a €45 billion Ukraine loan and 2028-2034 budget, as Germany threatens veto unless all members back the loan amid €70 billion funding gap disputes.

events.extended_summary: York Road in the Birmingham suburb of Kings Heath has been included among the world's coolest streets, recognized for its buzzy community atmosphere, independent shops, restaurants, and al-fresco vibe. The pedestrianised street features picnic benches and colourful painted shop fronts where pub tables spill across the road. The Grade II-listed Hare & Hounds pub, operating on the corner since 1907 and dating back to 1820, features Art Nouveau tiles and was the first venue where Birmingham reggae band UB40 played; other music venues include Fletchers and Schooners. Residents highlight the welcoming environment, with locals and visitors gathering to socialize, dance, and enjoy the street's unique character that distinguishes it from the city centre.
events.micro_summary: York Road in Kings Heath has been named one of the world's coolest streets.
events.summary: York Road in Birmingham's Kings Heath has been recognized as one of the world's coolest streets for its community atmosphere, independent shops, and the historic Hare & Hounds pub dating to 1820.

events.extended_summary: Severe weather threatens Thanksgiving travel for 81.5 million Americans, with 72.9 million driving. Pacific storms bring rain, snow, and winds to the West Coast, including an atmospheric river causing heavy rain from Washington to Northern California, delays on I-5 between Seattle and Sacramento, and impacts on I-80 and I-90. Highest tides of the year coincide with coastal flood watches. A southeast storm intensifies into a Nor'easter over Thanksgiving, affecting 250 million people across 25 states with floods, winds, and rain, prompting New York City to consider moving the 100th Macy's parade start. The Midwest prepares for a winter storm dropping close to a foot of snow in St. Louis, while Florida's Atlantic Coast faces more heavy rain.
events.micro_summary: Powerful storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel for 81.5 million Americans on both US coasts.
events.summary: Severe storms threaten Thanksgiving travel for 81.5 million Americans, with Pacific systems bringing rain and snow to the West Coast and a Nor'easter targeting the East Coast, potentially disrupting the Macy's parade and causing power outages across 25 states.

events.extended_summary: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for an immediate end to his corruption trial after judges recommended dropping the bribery case against him. In a televised statement at parliament, Netanyahu said the "fabricated cases" were falling apart and spoke of "ten years of terrible suffering" for him and his family. During a Jerusalem hearing, judges indicated little chance of conviction in Case 4000, which accuses Netanyahu of offering regulatory favors to a telecoms company for favorable media coverage, questioned whether Case 2000 actions amounted to criminal conduct, and suggested a plea deal for Case 1000. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara, unusually summoned to the hearing, said she would consider the recommendations. The developments come as Netanyahu fights for political survival after inconclusive October 27 elections, while opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's bloc voted for an independent investigation into the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack.
events.micro_summary: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu demanded an immediate end to his corruption trial after judges recommended dropping bribery charges.
events.summary: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for an immediate end to his corruption trial after judges recommended dropping the bribery case, questioning a second case, and suggesting a plea deal in a third.

events.extended_summary: The BBC has lodged an urgent appeal with the US Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit challenging a Florida federal judge's decision to allow Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit to proceed. The lawsuit concerns the editing of a Panorama documentary about Trump's speech on January 6, 2021, shortly before the Capitol riot. The BBC argues the Florida court lacks jurisdiction because the programme never aired in the United States and the broadcaster made rigorous efforts to prevent US access. Earlier this month, Judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled the case could continue, prompting Trump to call it a 'huge victory.' The BBC maintains there is a complete lack of evidence anyone in Florida viewed the documentary. Trump has been ordered to answer questions under oath by January 22, with a trial scheduled for May 3, 2027, in Fort Lauderdale.
events.micro_summary: The BBC has appealed a US court ruling allowing Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit to proceed.
events.summary: The BBC has filed an urgent appeal against a Florida judge's ruling allowing Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit to proceed, arguing the court lacks jurisdiction as the documentary never aired in the United States.

events.extended_summary: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday. The decision follows several incursions into Polish airspace that Poland blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods. The no-fly zone is intended to allow Polish forces to quickly identify any Russian military aircraft and shoot them down if necessary. The announcement comes as Poland continues to support Ukraine against the ongoing invasion while addressing repeated violations of its sovereign airspace.
events.micro_summary: Poland will create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border to shoot down Russian aircraft after airspace incursions.
events.summary: Poland announced it will soon establish a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border following several airspace incursions blamed on Russia, allowing forces to identify and shoot down Russian military aircraft if necessary.

events.extended_summary: Russian officials have dismissed proposals for NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine amid ongoing tensions between the two nations. Concurrently, Ukrainian naval drone strikes targeted Russian vessels in Libya. The Kremlin has ignored President Zelensky's ceasefire proposal while promoting a different humanitarian mission. Additionally, nuclear threats from Russia aim to deter Ukraine's military actions. These simultaneous developments, including the rejection of security guarantees, the naval drone strikes in Libya, the ignored ceasefire proposal, and the nuclear threats, underscore the continued escalation of military operations and the diplomatic impasse regarding security arrangements and ceasefire negotiations in the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine.
events.micro_summary: Russia dismisses Ukraine security guarantees and ignores ceasefire while Ukraine strikes Russian vessels in Libya.

sources.publisher: Institute for the Study of War

events.summary: Russian officials dismissed NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine and ignored President Zelensky's ceasefire proposal while promoting a separate humanitarian mission, as Ukrainian naval drones targeted Russian vessels in Libya and Russia issued nuclear threats to deter military actions.

events.extended_summary: Pakistan's first astronaut, 40-year-old Pakistan Air Force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, launched aboard China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft on Wednesday at 5:18am from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China, alongside Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi. The Long March-2F rocket lifted off before dawn, and the spacecraft separated and entered orbit about 10 minutes after liftoff. At 8:56am, the Shenzhou-24 docked at China's Tiangong space station, with the crew expected to enter at about 11:45am. Ali will conduct experiments in biotechnology and photosynthetic microorganisms during the five-day orbital flight before returning to Earth. The mission marks the first time China has sent a foreign national into space and coincides with 75 years of space cooperation between China and Pakistan. Observers in Islamabad watched the launch at the Pakistan Space & Upper Atmosphere Research Commission headquarters.
events.micro_summary: Pakistan's first astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali launched aboard China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft to the Tiangong space station.
events.summary: Pakistan's first astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali launched aboard China's Shenzhou-24 spacecraft from Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre on Wednesday, docking at the Tiangong space station at 8:56am for a five-day mission conducting experiments.

events.extended_summary: Up to 50 commercial shipping vessels were recently compromised by cyberattacks that U.S. officials suspect are linked to Iran. The breaches targeted ships carrying oil, liquefied gas, and explosive chemicals traveling across Asia and Europe, with several oil tankers headed toward the U.S. coast having their navigation systems breached in August. Hackers exploited known vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiGate devices, also known as FortiBleed, which are frequently used in the maritime industry to manage firewalls and virtual private networks. In August, the Coast Guard and FBI partnered to send a specialized team to board two foreign commercial vessels in the Gulf of America heading to U.S. ports. A joint FBI-Coast Guard cyber bulletin issued in September warned the industry about the threat. No operational disruptions, vessel instability, physical danger to crews, or environmental impacts have been observed, though dozens more ships in international waters are believed compromised.
events.micro_summary: Up to 50 commercial shipping vessels were compromised by cyberattacks suspected to be linked to Iran.
events.summary: Up to 50 commercial shipping vessels were recently compromised by cyberattacks suspected to be linked to Iran, exploiting vulnerabilities in Fortinet devices, with no current operational disruptions or physical danger to crews.

events.extended_summary: Unknown attackers breached an unclassified open-source intelligence analysis system used by the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency also affected. Officials confirmed no classified information or critical capabilities were disrupted, and no classified systems were compromised. Investigators suspect the hackers used the open-source AI hacking tool Artex, which significantly reduces the time required to carry out cyberattack stages by automating the process with artificial intelligence. Early indications suggest the attack may have originated in China, though it remains unclear whether the country's government was involved. The full extent of the breach, when it occurred, and whether it has been resolved remain unknown. The incident does not appear related to a separate apparent hack of the FBI's nationwide criminal information database.
events.micro_summary: CIA, ODNI and NGA systems breached via AI tool Artex, affecting unclassified data only.
events.summary: Unknown attackers breached unclassified open-source intelligence systems at the CIA, ODNI, and NGA using the AI tool Artex, with early indications pointing to China, though no classified information was affected.

events.extended_summary: Liverpool recovered from a shock defeat to Fenerbahce to beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League league phase. Alexander Isak scored twice, opening the scoring following a misplaced pass from Yann Sommer and adding a late chipped finish to take his season tally to 10 goals. Florian Wirtz scored the second goal with a finish at the near post after a surging run from Rio Ngumoha. The victory was Liverpool's fourth in five league phase matches, moving them up to fifth in the standings. Victor Munoz suffered an injury in the first half after clattering into a defender and was replaced by Ngumoha. Club Brugge's Felix Lemarechal was the hosts' greatest threat, forcing saves from Alisson, but could not prevent the defeat.
events.micro_summary: Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League with Alexander Isak scoring twice.
events.summary: Liverpool defeated Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League, with Alexander Isak scoring twice and Florian Wirtz adding another, moving Liverpool to fifth in the league phase standings with their fourth win in five games.

events.extended_summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers released veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers following a public dispute with head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers, 43, was benched for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos after claiming McCarthy fell asleep during meetings and missed offensive sessions. In media interviews, Rodgers detailed instances where McCarthy allegedly snored during a quarterback meeting and left early. The Steelers confirmed Rodgers would be inactive despite McCarthy previously stating he remained the starter. Mason Rudolph is set to start in Rodgers' place. The four-time NFL MVP had previously stated that the word "benched" never came up in discussions with McCarthy. Meanwhile, the Minnesota Vikings, who had considered signing Rodgers before the 2025 season, avoided the situation after dialogue failed to produce a contract.
events.micro_summary: Aaron Rodgers released by Pittsburgh Steelers after benching and public criticism of coach Mike McCarthy.
events.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers released quarterback Aaron Rodgers after benching him for Friday's game against Denver and following his public claims that head coach Mike McCarthy fell asleep in meetings. Mason Rudolph will start in his place.

events.extended_summary: The Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams will play on Wednesday, November 25 at 7 p.m. CT at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The game will be broadcast on Netflix, with local over-the-air television available on NBC26 in the Green Bay market and TMJ4 in the Milwaukee market, and streaming available on NFL+ for mobile devices. Both teams enter the matchup with 6-4 records. The Packers will welcome back star defensive end Micah Parsons, who makes his season debut following an ACL tear suffered last December. The Rams will be without All-Pro wide receiver Puka Nacua, who is out for the rest of the season with a knee injury. The game can also be heard on the Packers Radio Network across 54 stations in six states, with the flagship station at 95.7 BIG FM.
events.micro_summary: Green Bay Packers face Los Angeles Rams Wednesday at SoFi Stadium with both teams at 6-4.
events.summary: The Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams meet Wednesday at 7 p.m. CT at SoFi Stadium in a game broadcast on Netflix, with both teams holding 6-4 records.

events.extended_summary: North Melbourne will play Melbourne in its fourth consecutive AFLW grand final, aiming to become the first side in competition history to secure a three-peat. The Kangaroos have lost just one game in their last 43 matches and boast a 96 per cent winning rate since losing the 2023 grand final. A victory would equal Adelaide's record of three premierships in the competition. This marks the first year neither Adelaide nor Brisbane will feature in the grand final. Brisbane has played in seven grand finals with two wins, while Adelaide currently holds the record with three premierships. North Melbourne has only lost once in the past three AFLW seasons. The dominance is viewed as beneficial for the league's long-term competitiveness as other teams work to close the gap.
events.micro_summary: North Melbourne aims for historic AFLW three-peat against Melbourne in fourth consecutive grand final.

sources.publisher: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

events.summary: North Melbourne faces Melbourne in the AFLW grand final seeking a historic third consecutive premiership, which would equal Adelaide's record of three titles. The Kangaroos have lost only once in their last 43 matches.

events.extended_summary: Huge fire erupts near Cairo killing at least 30 people Thirty-one people have been killed and 21 others injured in a large fire on a busy highway in Cairo after a fuel tanker crashed, Egypt's health ministry says. Hospitals nearby treated patients suffering burns and smoke inhalation after the incident, which occurred on a section of a ring road in the Warraq neighbourhood, to the north of the old city centre, on Wednesday evening. Footage circulating on social media showed billowing flames and black smoke towering high into the night sky, with multiple nearby vehicles torched. Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol. events.micro_summary: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway.
events.summary: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway. Officials have not given an account of how the fire broke out, but state-owned media reported the tanker had overturned, dousing nearby vehicles with petrol.

events.extended_summary: A Cessna 210 plane crashed into the Gulf of Mexico two nautical miles northeast of Horn Island off the Mississippi coast Tuesday afternoon around 3:30 p.m., killing all six people on board. The aircraft departed New Orleans Lakefront Airport en route to Fort Myers, Florida, after the family completed a fishing trip in southeastern Louisiana. The victims were pilot Brent Stokes, 50; his son Hunter Stokes, 16; Brent's sister Arlyn Knox, 43; her husband Michael Knox, 43; and their sons Charles Holden Knox, 12, and Truett Knox, 10. The plane was flying in fair weather when it began dropping at 10,000 feet per minute. Coast Guard responders searched through the night, finding the cabin, three life jackets and a life raft before divers recovered the bodies from the fuselage. The Federal Aviation Administration and National Transportation Safety Board launched investigations into the cause.
events.micro_summary: Six people died when a Cessna 210 crashed into the Gulf of Mexico off Mississippi Tuesday.
events.summary: A Cessna 210 crashed into the Gulf of Mexico off Horn Island, Mississippi, Tuesday, killing six people including three children. The family was returning to Fort Myers, Florida, from a fishing trip. Federal authorities are investigating.

events.extended_summary: Former Australian police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been unanimously found guilty of murdering TV presenter Jesse Baird, 26, and Baird's boyfriend Luke Davies, 29, in Sydney on 19 February 2024. The jury rejected Lamarre-Condon's claims that he acted in self-defense and that the second shot was accidental. He was also convicted of breaking and entering and stealing. Eight days after the killings, the victims' bodies were discovered in surfboard bags near a monastery in rural Bungonia, south-west of Sydney. Lamarre-Condon admitted moving the bodies in a hired van and attempting to sink them in a farm dam using cement and weights. The nine-week trial heard that Lamarre-Condon's relationship with Baird was marked by jealousy and controlling behavior after they separated in April 2023. He will be sentenced in March 2027.
events.micro_summary: Former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon was found guilty of murdering TV presenter Jesse Baird and his boyfriend Luke Davies.
events.summary: A jury unanimously convicted former Australian police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, of murdering TV presenter Jesse Baird and flight attendant Luke Davies in Sydney in February 2024, rejecting his self-defense claims.

events.extended_summary: Macy's has postponed its 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City from Thursday to Saturday due to a powerful nor'easter threatening the region with heavy rain and winds gusting up to 60mph. City regulations require the parade's 100 giant character balloons to be grounded if sustained winds exceed 23mph or gusts surpass 35mph, making Thursday's conditions too dangerous. The balloons, including 10 new inflatables, were deflated Wednesday night and stored in New Jersey for reinflation before Saturday's event. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed the decision, citing safety as paramount and noting an expanded police presence along the route. The parade, featuring marching bands and floats, has only been cancelled during World War II between 1942 and 1944, making this the first weather-related postponement in its history.
events.micro_summary: Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday due to severe nor'easter winds.
events.summary: Macy's 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York has been postponed from Thursday to Saturday due to a powerful nor'easter bringing winds up to 60mph, forcing the deflation of 100 giant balloons for safety.

events.extended_summary: Netflix's first Pakistani series, "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo," has triggered a cross-border controversy ahead of its scheduled December 4 release. The trailer, featuring actors Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan and Sanam Saeed, was released Tuesday, though it remains unclear whether the release will include India. In India, the All Indian Cine Workers Association and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging him to block the series, citing a May 8, 2025 Ministry of Information and Broadcasting advisory that asked OTT platforms to discontinue Pakistani-origin content following the Pahalgam terror attack. The associations described Pakistan as a "terrorist country" and argued the release would violate the advisory. Meanwhile, Pakistan's Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal criticised the ban calls on X using the hashtag #GrowUpIndia, accusing New Delhi of weaponising art and culture. Netflix has maintained silence.
events.micro_summary: Netflix's first Pakistani series triggers controversy with Indian bodies seeking ban before December 4 release.
events.summary: Netflix's first Pakistani series "Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo" triggers controversy as Indian bodies urge PM Modi to block its December 4 release while Pakistan accuses India of weaponising art.

events.extended_summary: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya addressed the 16th edition of the Global Summit on the Business of Sports TURF-2026 in New Delhi, stating that schemes including Khelo India Mission, Fit India Movement and Target Olympic Podium Scheme are expanding grassroots participation and identifying talent. He highlighted the transformation of India's sporting ecosystem over the past 12 years under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with a vision to become a global sports ecosystem. The government has approved a sports goods manufacturing scheme with an outlay of nearly two thousand crore rupees to make India a global hub for manufacturing and innovation. Mandaviya also noted preparations for the Commonwealth Games 2030 and India's ambition to host the 2036 Olympic Games, while France serves as the partner country with a signed MoU for cooperation.
events.micro_summary: Dr Mansukh Mandaviya announced a nearly two thousand crore rupees scheme and 2036 Olympic bid at TURF-2026 in New Delhi.
events.summary: Dr Mansukh Mandaviya addressed the 16th TURF-2026 summit in New Delhi, citing 12 years of sporting growth, a nearly two thousand crore rupees manufacturing scheme, and ambitions for the 2036 Olympics and 2030 Commonwealth Games.

events.extended_summary: The September 2025 Gen Z protests precipitated a historic political transition in Nepal, bringing a young cabinet led by former Kathmandu Mayor Balendra Shah to power.[1] India’s fundamental importance to Nepal remains unchanged, but the new political dispensation has brought fresh expectations to the bilateral relationship. In this regard, PM Shah’s visit to India on 22–23 November 2026, his first bilateral visit since assuming office in March, marks an important engagement. For India, the visit provided an opportunity to engage directly with the new leadership in Kathmandu. For Nepal, it offered an avenue to advance its domestic development priorities, particularly economic recovery and reconstruction following the devastating August 2026 floods. More broadly, the visit provided an opportunity to reassess a relationship that, despite its historical and geographical foundations, has periodically encountered political differences over territorial issues, the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, trade and transit arrangements, and perceptions of
events.micro_summary: Prime Minister Balen Shah’s Visit and India–Nepal Relations.
events.summary: Prime Minister Balen Shah’s Visit and India–Nepal Relations. In this regard, PM Shah’s visit to India on 22–23 November 2026, his first bilateral visit since assuming office in March, marks an important engagement.

events.extended_summary: Researchers at IIT Guwahati have developed a new method for seismic hazard assessment in Northeast India, compiling a catalogue of nearly 6,000 earthquakes over the past 1,200 years and generating 200 synthetic earthquake catalogues using Kernel Density Estimation and geological fault orientations. The study identified the Indo-Burma Ranges as having the most intense earthquake activity, with Imphal showing the highest estimated ground shaking among eight major cities including Guwahati, Agartala, Shillong, Aizawl, Kohima, Gangtok and Itanagar. Northeast India lies between two tectonic boundaries and contains the Shillong Plateau and numerous geological faults, making it prone to earthquakes such as the devastating 1897 Shillong and 1950 Assam events. The methodology accounts for non-uniform seismic activity and historical data inaccuracies, providing crucial information for engineers to design earthquake-resistant buildings, bridges and infrastructure in the vulnerable region.
events.micro_summary: IIT Guwahati researchers developed a seismic hazard method using nearly 6,000 earthquakes to predict ground shaking in Northeast India.
events.summary: IIT Guwahati researchers developed a new seismic hazard assessment method for Northeast India using nearly 6,000 earthquakes from the past 1,200 years, identifying Imphal as having the highest estimated ground shaking among eight major cities to aid resilient construction.
